objective.text: Point the web document root at public so application source and environment files are not directly served.

difficulty.rationale: Expose the intended front controller without serving the private application tree.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

stem: A web-server configuration points its document root at the Laravel project root and makes .env downloadable. Which deployment boundary should replace that setup?

options.text: Keep the project root and rename .env to a less predictable filename only.
options.rationale: Obscuring one filename does not establish the intended public/private directory boundary.
options.misconception: Obscuring one filename does not establish the intended public/private directory boundary.

options.text: Keep the project root and add Laravel middleware that rejects requests for dotfiles.
options.rationale: The web server may serve a file before Laravel middleware runs; the document-root boundary must be correct.
options.misconception: The web server may serve a file before Laravel middleware runs; the document-root boundary must be correct.

options.text: Serve the application through its public directory as the document root.
options.rationale: The public directory contains the web entry point and public assets; private application files should not be exposed by serving the project root.

options.text: Point at the project root and remove read access to .env only.
options.rationale: Restricting one file still exposes other private application paths; serving through public establishes the intended boundary.
options.misconception: Restricting one file still exposes other private application paths; serving through public establishes the intended boundary.

validation.reason: Laravel publicPath defaults to the public subtree; official deployment guidance requires serving through public/index.php. No web-server configuration is changed or penetration-tested.
